items.subject: Archimedean
notes: D6 resolved: no Interface/Definitions folder — Archimedean is a property of an existing (Add,LT,OfNat 0) signature, not a new operation bundle, matching the precedent of other order-compatibility-style atomic laws elsewhere in the tree. Interface/Laws/Definition.lean only.

Audited: ArchimedeanLaw (multiples of x cofinal under < for x>0) matches the user's ordered-group/ordered-field formulation (#1/#2 of their spec) exactly, confirmed via Cofinal's definition. Content unchanged, moved as-is.

Noted, not a bug: IteratedSelfSum is one-indexed (IteratedSelfSum 0 x = x = 1*x in nsmul terms), harmless for the cofinality property since 0 is never a needed witness except for point<0, which n=0 (i.e. x itself) already covers.

Constructions/Mathlib/Laws.lean: real bridge from Mathlib's own `Archimedean` class (ordered add comm monoids) — required an actual reindexing lemma (IteratedSelfSum n x = (n+1)*nsmul) and a strict-vs-non-strict adaptation (Mathlib's arch is <=, ours needs <), both proved, not sorry'd (structural glue).

Examples/: Integers, Rationals — both `example : ArchimedeanLaw _ := inferInstance`, for free via the Mathlib bridge once the right concrete-instance-providing import (Mathlib.Algebra.Order.Archimedean.Basic) is pulled in.

DEFERRED, flagged for the user: a Failures/ non-Archimedean counterexample (e.g. lexicographically-ordered Z x Z, or the rational-function field ℝ(x) the user's spec discussed) was not built this item — real extra construction work (a full ordered structure from scratch), not audit/reorg. Worth a dedicated follow-up if wanted.

items.subject: DiscreteInteger
notes: User-supplied spec: three equivalent characterizations of Z -- (1) two-sided Peano/System SP (0, Succ, Pred, invertibility, acyclicity, bidirectional induction), (2) free infinite cyclic group (universal algebra view), (3) discretely ordered ring / Presburger completeness. The six pre-existing independent classes (HasSuccessor, HasPredecessor, SuccessorLaws, SuccessorAdditionLaw, SuccessorMultiplicationLaws, DiscretenessLaw) already correspond to definition (1) plus a bridge to (3)'s ring structure; kept that shape per D6, did not attempt to also build out (2)'s free-group presentation or (3)'s full Presburger quantifier-elimination content -- out of scope, new math beyond an audit/reorg pass.

AUDIT BUG FOUND AND FIXED (D2 risk, on this item too): DiscretenessLaw's SuccAperiodic field was quantified only at the basepoint (SuccIterate n (0:R) != 0), not universally as the user's own acyclicity axiom states (forall x, forall n>0, S^n(x) != x). The narrower statement typechecked and looked plausible but is strictly weaker/different -- without extra additive structure nothing forces the basepoint's aperiodicity to transfer to every other element. Fixed: SuccAperiodic (both the class field and its Wrappers-section restated theorem) now quantifies over an explicit x : R matching the spec verbatim. SuccInjective/PredInjective in SuccessorLaws were also reviewed -- these ARE provable consequences of the two invertibility fields rather than independent axioms, but are true and kept as bundled fields for interface convenience, not a bug (noted in the new doc comment).

Reorg: Definition.lean + Laws/Definition.lean (six classes + a Wrappers section of restated theorems, all already sorry'd pre-session) relocated into Interface/{Definitions,Laws}, matching the rest of the tree. DiscreteInteger kept as ONE Laws/Definition.lean file (not split per-class into separate files) since the six classes were already coexisting in one file with no issues -- matches Archimedean's single-file precedent for a subject with no single combining law.

ConceptSignature (Interface/Definitions/ConceptSignature.lean) still extends RingConceptSignature (tier 5's Ring) -- a UA-signature-level dependency, not a Laws-level one, so it doesn't affect D5's tier ordering (which only tracks Laws/Definition.lean imports) or block this item from being tier 1. Left as-is, pre-existing, not touched beyond the folder move -- flagged here as a known oddity worth a second look whenever Ring (as-24) itself gets reorged.

No Constructions/ folder built this item, unlike every prior item -- HasSuccessor/ HasPredecessor/DiscretenessLaw are LRA-specific classes with no single matching generic Mathlib typeclass to bridge from (unlike Group/SemilatticeSup/Archimedean's 1-1 Mathlib counterparts); Z is also essentially the *only* model per the user's own categoricity framing, so a generic multi-carrier bridge wouldn't buy much. Built Examples/Integers.lean directly instead: concrete HasSuccessor/HasPredecessor instances on Int (Succ := (+1), Pred := (-1)) plus instances of all four Prop classes, all sorry'd from the start per D8.

Import-path fixes: AlgebraicStructures/MathlibBridge.lean, NumberSystems/{IntegerStructure,PeanoSystem}/Interface/ModelTheory/LStructure.lean (.Laws.Definition -> .Interface.Laws.Definition, three consumers outside this item's own subject tree -- more than prior items typically touch), VolumeVICore.lean (.Laws -> .Interface.Laws), VolumeVIExamplesFailures.lean (dropped the now-deleted .Laws.Examples stub import, .Examples import unchanged).

validate_structure.py passes on DiscreteInteger and the full AlgebraicStructures tree. lake build (DiscreteInteger + Examples + MathlibBridge + both LStructure.lean consumers + VolumeVICore + VolumeVIExamplesFailures + full AlgebraicStructures umbrella) all pass clean, 1932 jobs on the umbrella-plus-consumers set.

items.subject: JoinSemilattice
notes: D6 resolved (important, see DECISIONS.md): the flat def-with-explicit-operation-argument style is DELIBERATE, not a lapse to fix toward class-based [Mul R] uniformity. Lattice needs join AND meet as two independent operations coexisting on one carrier at once, which a single instance-per-type typeclass parameter cannot express. Converting JoinSemilattice to [Mul R] style would have broken Lattice. Kept the style, just relocated into Interface/{Definitions,Laws}.

Audited: JoinSemilatticeLaws = Associative + Commutative + Idempotent on the explicit `join` operation, exactly matching the user's algebraic definition (equivalently, an idempotent commutative semigroup). A separate, pre-existing order-theoretic definition lives at LRA.Order.Lattices.JoinSemilattice (poset+suprema) — no bridge between the two exists yet, flagged as future Interop work, out of scope for this reorg pass.

Constructions/Mathlib/Laws.lean: ofSemilatticeSup, a plain theorem (not an instance!) that [SemilatticeSup R] gives JoinSemilatticeLaws (·⊔·) — safe because it never touches Mul/Add at all, so none of the usual instance-diamond risk applies here.

Examples/: UnionSemilattice (Set union, direct), RealsUnderMax (ℝ max, via the Mathlib bridge) — both prove the explicit-function form directly, no wrapper structs needed since there's no Mul-instance to avoid colliding with.
Import-path fix: Lattice/Laws/Definition.lean, VolumeVICore.lean (.Laws -> .Interface.Laws)

FOLLOW-UP same day: user asked for the missing bridge to the order-theoretic definition. Added Constructions/OrderTheoretic/InducedOrder.lean: InducedOrder join := fun x y => join x y = y, proved (not sorry'd -- Constructions are structural glue, same precedent as ClosedSubset builders) that it's a genuine LRA.Order.PartialOrder (reflexivity=idempotence, antisymmetry=commutativity, transitivity=associativity) and that `join left right` really is the least upper bound (LRA.Order.Join), concluding toOrderTheoreticJoinSemilattice : JoinSemilatticeLaws join -> LRA.Order.JoinSemilattice (InducedOrder join) -- the actual equivalence-of-definitions theorem from the user's spec, built and proved in full, first try, no errors.

validate_structure.py + lake build (JoinSemilattice + Lattice.Laws + VolumeVICore/VolumeVIExamplesFailures + full AlgebraicStructures umbrella) all pass, 1671 jobs (1503 after the OrderTheoretic addition)

CORRECTED 2026-08-26 per D8: inducedOrder_isPartialOrder and inducedOrder_hasJoins (the actual order-theory content, and the proof that triggered the D8 correction in the first place) reverted to sorry. toOrderTheoreticJoinSemilattice stays as a plain composition of the two (now-sorry) lemmas, no separate proof of its own. ofSemilatticeSup (the Mathlib bridge one-liner) reverted to sorry too, per D8's explicit no-exceptions rule.

CORRECTED AGAIN 2026-08-26 (as-09 session): Examples/UnionSemilattice.lean's unionIsJoinSemilattice theorem was missed by the prior D8 sweep -- it was still proved in full despite this ledger entry's own prior claim that as-08's Examples proofs were reverted. Reverted to sorry. lake build re-verified clean (LRA.AlgebraicStructures.JoinSemilattice.Examples).
